reasoning: Recent Alaska Senate polling in the last 45 days is mixed: a June 15-29 NYT/Siena poll showed Republican Dan Sullivan up 2, while an Alaska Survey Research poll from June 4-7 showed Democrat Mary Peltola up 5.2; polling averages cited by aggregate sites now put the race near toss-up, with a slight Republican edge to a small Democratic edge depending on the aggregator. Cook’s statewide PVI for Alaska is R+9, so the state remains structurally Republican even as the Senate race is competitive.

sources.name: The New York Times / Siena College
sources.details: NYT/Siena found Sullivan leading Peltola 47% to 45% among likely voters in Alaska’s Senate race.

sources.name: Alaska Survey Research
sources.details: Alaska Survey Research found Peltola leading Sullivan 49.4% to 44.2% in the Senate race.

sources.name: PollsMax polling average
sources.details: A polling average for Alaska’s Senate race showed Sullivan ahead 46.7% to 45.8%, a Republican edge of 0.9 points.

sources.name: Alaska News
sources.details: The article says Alaska’s Senate contest is being treated as a toss-up by Cook Political Report and that mid-2026 polling shows Peltola ahead by five to seven points in some surveys.

sources.name: Cook Political Report PVI
sources.details: Cook Political Report’s statewide partisan baseline for Alaska is R+9.
